idea.body: A two-step equation changes the unknown twice, so it takes two opposite operations, in reverse order, to undo it. Undo the addition or subtraction first, then undo the multiplication or division last, the reverse of how the equation was built. If 3x + 4 = 19, subtract 4 from both sides to get 3x = 15, then divide by 3 to get x = 5. A game gives a starting bonus of 7 points plus 12 points per level cleared. A final score of 91 gives the equation 12x + 7 = 91, and solving it gives x = 7 levels. Always undo the loosest, outermost operation before the one holding the unknown.

workedExample.prompt: A game gives a starting bonus of 7 points plus 12 points for every level cleared. Its final score is 91. Solve 12x + 7 = 91 for x, the number of levels cleared.
steps: A game gives a starting bonus of 7 points plus 12 points for every level cleared.
The final score is 91, so 12x + 7 = 91.
Undo the addition first: subtract 7 from both sides to get 12x = 84.
Undo the multiplication last: divide both sides by 12.
x = 7, so the player cleared 7 levels.

ways.name: Undo in reverse order
ways.when: Use this for any two-step equation as the default, reliable method.
steps: 3x + 4 = 19 was built by multiplying by 3 first, then adding 4.
Undo the addition first: subtract 4 from both sides to get 3x = 15.
Undo the multiplication last: divide both sides by 3.
ways.trap: Dividing by 3 before subtracting 4, undoing the steps out of order.

ways.name: Cover-up working backward
ways.when: Use this when you want to solve in two quick fact questions instead of formal steps.
steps: Cover the whole multiplication part: [box] - 3 = 17.
What must the box be? 17 + 3 = 20, so 4x = 20.
Now cover just x: 4 times [box] = 20, so the box is 5.
ways.trap: Solving for the covered part but forgetting to divide by 4 to reach x.

ways.name: Guess, check and adjust
ways.when: Use this when the equation has small, friendly numbers to test.
steps: Guess x = 5 and check: 2 times 5 plus 5 = 15, too small.
Try a bigger number, x = 7: 2 times 7 plus 5 = 19, too big now.
Adjust between 5 and 7: try x = 6. 2 times 6 plus 5 = 17, which matches.
ways.trap: Adjusting by too large a jump and skipping past the answer.

ways.name: The function machine
ways.when: Use this to picture the equation as steps built forward, then undone backward.
steps: Picture the equation as a machine: x goes in, gets multiplied by 5, then has 2 subtracted, and 13 comes out.
To undo it, run the machine backward from 13: first add 2, undoing the subtraction, giving 15.
Then divide by 5, undoing the multiplication, giving 3.
ways.trap: Running the backward steps in the same order as the forward machine instead of reversed.
